questions.q: Which config file section holds settings for the MySQL server process itself?
options: [mysqld]
[client]
[server-process]
[global]
questions.explain: [mysqld] configures the server process; [client] configures command-line client defaults.

questions.q: What's the difference between SHOW VARIABLES and SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES?
options: SHOW VARIABLES returns the current session's values; SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES always returns the server-wide value
They always return identical results
SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES only works for InnoDB settings
SHOW VARIABLES requires root privileges and SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES does not
questions.explain: Session values can diverge from global values if a session changes its own copy of a variable.

questions.q: If you run SET GLOBAL max_connections = 500; but never update my.cnf, what happens on the next server restart?
options: The setting reverts to whatever my.cnf specifies, since SET GLOBAL alone isn't persisted
The setting stays at 500 permanently
The server fails to start
MySQL automatically writes the change to my.cnf
questions.explain: SET GLOBAL changes the running server but is not automatically written to the config file.

questions.q: What does SET PERSIST do differently from a plain SET GLOBAL, since MySQL 8.0?
options: It writes the changed variable to mysqld-auto.cnf so it survives a restart
It only changes the value for the current session
It requires editing my.cnf manually afterward
It has no functional difference from SET GLOBAL
questions.explain: SET PERSIST persists the global variable change across restarts without manually editing the config file.

questions.q: What does SET SESSION sql_mode = 'STRICT_TRANS_TABLES'; affect?
options: Only the current connection; the value disappears when that connection closes
Every connection on the server, immediately
The my.cnf file directly
Only new connections established after the command runs
questions.explain: SET SESSION (or plain SET) scopes the change to the current connection only.
